candidates.changed_node: graft: TS_MIN($low, 21) floor (from A) over a TS_SUM($high - $low, 21) denominator, multiplied by CS_DEMEAN(-TS_RANK($high - $low, 42)) built from B's range leg
candidates.rationale: Fusion is a conditioner plus a normaliser swap. A measures where price sits in its 21-day range but normalises by the same extremum range it measures position in; B never looks at position at all, only at whether the daily range is wide for this name. The child keeps A's floor reference, rescales the distance above it by cumulative true range (the archive's own evidence: TS_MEAN/TS_SUM($high-$low,w) denominators carry accepts while TS_MAX-TS_MIN denominators screen out), and then signs the whole thing by B's within-name range percentile: high in the range on a compressed tape is a squeeze breakout, high in the range on an expanded tape is exhaustion. Neither parent has that interaction. Donations: TS_MIN($low, 21) from A and $high - $low from B, 3 nodes each; A's $close - TS_MIN($low,21) (5 nodes) is replaced by a TS_MEAN($close,5) numerator and B's TS_RANK($high-$low,10) (5 nodes) is re-windowed, so no 4+ node block of either parent survives. The range-position family is saturated (A's 126-day twin was rejected at rho 0.858, a TS_MAX/TS_SUM restatement at 0.965), which is exactly why the positive position term is multiplied by a CS_DEMEAN'd percentile: a zero-mean multiplier drives covariance with A toward zero, where a strictly positive rank would retain about 0.87 of it.

candidates.changed_node: combinator change: B's CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) multiplied by, rather than differenced against, a demeaned TS_RANK over A's $high - $low
candidates.rationale: This is a weak pair and I want to say so: both parents are a ROE rank minus a range-derived term, so they share their fundamental leg outright and differ only in how the range term is measured (A's within-name percentile vs B's cross-sectional rank of volume/range comovement). The one fusion I can name honestly is a change of combinator, not of content: turn the spread into an interaction, so the quality premium is scaled and sign-flipped by the name's own volatility state rather than having a volatility rank subtracted from it. That does capture something neither parent does (quality paying differently in compressed vs expanded tape) but it is a thin cross compared with pairs 5-8. Donations: $high - $low from A and CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) from B, 3 nodes each; B's 7-node CS_RANK(TS_CORR(...)) leg and A's TS_RANK($high-$low,10) are both dropped. The decorrelation bet is specific and evidence-backed: the archive already rejected CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) * TS_RANK(($high-$open)/($dollar_volume+1e-8), 42) at rho 0.883, and three more variants at 0.869-0.984, all against CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) * CS_RANK(TS_MEAN($high-$low,10)/...). Every one of those multiplied the quality leg by a strictly positive rank, which keeps roughly E[r]/sqrt(E[r^2]) ~ 0.87 of the shared leg. Demeaning the second factor reduces that to cov(s,r)/0.167, i.e. below 0.5 even if the two range measures correlate at 0.9.

candidates.changed_node: graft: B's TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) normalised by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 63) and z-scored, replacing A's CS_RANK(TS_CORR(...)) penalty with a multiplicative flow conditioner
candidates.rationale: The conditioning variable is dollar-flow acceleration. A prices quality against a contemporaneous volume/range comovement level and says nothing about whether flow into the name is rising or draining; B measures the 5-day change in dollar volume but carries no fundamental at all. The child asks whether the ROE premium concentrates in names whose traded value is accelerating relative to their own three-month norm, and flips sign for quality names the tape is abandoning. Dividing B's raw flow shock by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 63) is not cosmetic: a raw TS_DELTA($dollar_volume,5) ranks large caps to the top by construction, so the ratio is what makes the leg a shock rather than a size proxy. Donations: CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) from A and TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) from B, 3 nodes each; A's 6-node TS_CORR($volume, $high-$low, 15) and B's 8-node correlation kernel are both gone. Both factors are zero-centred, so this is a genuine interaction rather than a tilt, which is what keeps it off the saturated CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) * <positive rank> chassis that has drawn four correlation rejections at 0.869-0.984.

candidates.changed_node: graft: B's TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) wrapped in a within-name TS_RANK at A's 63-day horizon, multiplied against A's demeaned turnover rank
candidates.rationale: The interaction is capital efficiency times unusual flow, measured at A's horizon on B's variable. A pairs the asset-turnover tilt with a slow 63-day volume/range comovement; B has a fast 5-day flow shock and no fundamental. The child keeps A's 63-day window but repurposes it as the lookback for a within-name percentile of B's flow shock, so the question becomes: is this efficient operator drawing dollar flow that is unusual by its own quarter-long standard? TS_RANK is computed within the name, so unlike a cross-sectional rank of a raw delta it carries no size loading. Donations: CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($asset_turnover)) from A and TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) from B, 3 nodes each; A's CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high-$low, 63)) leg is dropped entirely. candidates.changed_node: graft: A's TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5), scaled by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21), enters B's MIN conjunction in place of the asset-turnover delta leg
candidates.rationale: The fusion is confirmation by flow, expressed as a strict conjunction. B identifies accrual-clean fundamental improvement but has no way to tell whether the market has begun to act on it; A identifies where dollar flow is accelerating but cannot tell whether the flow is justified by anything. MIN scores a name only when both hold, isolating the confirmed-improvement cohort that neither parent can select. It also reuses B's own combinator, moved across domains: B takes MIN over two fundamental deltas, the child takes it over one fundamental and one flow leg. B's accrual penalty is folded into the improvement term as a single raw difference (precedent in the archive: CS_RANK($roa - $accrual_gap)), which is what keeps B's 4-node CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($roa, 63)) block from being restated - that block on its own is enough to trip the subtree gate. Donations: TS_DELTA($roa, 63) from B and TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) from A, 3 nodes each. The flow leg is divided by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) because a bare cross-sectional rank of a dollar-volume delta is close to a size rank.

candidates.changed_node: graft: B's TS_DELTA($roa, 63), demeaned, becomes the multiplicative weight on a 21-over-126 day log momentum rebuilt from A's DELAY($close, 21)
candidates.rationale: This is the cleanest cross of the eight: A is risk-adjusted skip-month price momentum with no fundamental input, B is fundamental change with no price input, and the child is their interaction. Skip-month log momentum is signed and sized by the cross-sectionally demeaned quarterly ROA change, so the factor is long trends the fundamentals confirm and short trends that diverge from them - the conditioning neither parent can express. I will flag the known weakness of a pure product: the agree-down quadrant (deteriorating ROA, falling price) also scores positive, so the factor is really a directional-agreement measure rather than a one-sided momentum filter. Donations: DELAY($close, 21) from A and TS_DELTA($roa, 63) from B, 3 nodes each. candidates.changed_node: graft: B's TS_STD($return, 63) inverted into a long-over-short vol term structure and used as a multiplicative gain on A's TS_DELTA($asset_turnover, 63)
candidates.rationale: The normaliser is the fusion. A ranks fundamental improvement flat across the panel, treating every name's improvement as equally informative; B uses the short-over-long volatility term structure only as a static penalty subtracted from a quality rank. The child turns that term structure into a gain on A's improvement signal: a turnover improvement is upweighted when the name's recent realised vol is compressed relative to its long-run level, the quiet regime where the news is least likely to be priced already, and downweighted when recent vol is elevated. Two mechanical constraints shaped the windows: B's TS_STD($return, 63) + 1e-8 is a 5-node block so the guard had to move to the other leg, and the 21-day guard is taken by an existing member's TS_MEAN($return,21)/(TS_STD($return,21) + 1e-8), leaving 10. The CS_RANK sits outside the whole product rather than on the delta, so A's CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($asset_turnover, 63)) 4-node block is never formed.

candidates.changed_node: graft: A's TS_STD($return, 5) vs TS_STD($return, 63) comparison becomes an IF_ELSE regime switch on the sign of B's TS_SUM($return, 10)
candidates.rationale: Both parents describe return shape - A the volatility term structure, B the efficiency of the 10-day move - and both attach it to the same ROA rank, but neither lets one govern the other. The child makes A's term structure a regime switch on B's net move: follow the 10-day drift when short-run vol sits below the long-run level, fade it when short-run vol is elevated, since short-horizon reversal concentrates in turbulent tape while quiet drift persists. Quality then weights the position. That switch is the conditioning neither parent has; A's ratio only ever penalises, B's efficiency ratio treats every regime alike. prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.
